notes: S7 ADDITION, and it exists to fix a rule this project had already written down and then broke. contract.hpp says 'not one proper noun in this file's output was chosen by a programmer'; the Gilded Gull's final warning was a hardcoded English sentence sitting in tavern.cpp, composed by whoever wrote the door policy. It is here now, with three rows instead of one, so a bouncer does not say the same sentence to every player on every night of the ward's life. Same rule every other bark file obeys: NOTHING in the code writes a spoken line. The keys resolve through the same fallback chain barks.json uses, and this file is loaded after the owner's own, so it can never take a key of theirs.

rows: That is your one. Out of this house.
You have had the only word you get. The door.
I said it once. There is no second time in here.
Out. Master Venn keeps a quiet room and you are not it.
You were told. Mind the step.
Out you go, and the step is not my fault.
Walk or be carried. Either way it is the same door.
The penny falls at quarter-day and the Flame keeps the roll, not me.
Ground rent. Not for the house - the house is yours. For the dirt under it.
Pay the Duke or lease him the year. Those are the two ways it has ever gone.
Two quarters behind. He has been patient and patience is a thing men run out of.
The roll says what the roll says. You are on the wrong side of it.
He offered terms. That is the part the priest will ask about.
Bondsworn, then. Your wage is his and your work is his yard.
You kept the house and sold the years. Most would call that the better half.
Board and biscuit, set low, and the arrears come off a little each quarter.
Worked out and blessed. The Flame does that part cheap and it is worth a great deal.
Discharged. Nobody holds paper on you this morning.
Your wage is your own again. Do not sign the next one in a hungry quarter.
Father Maell hears it at the Mission. He weighs the tenant, not the ledger.
The offering is an offering. It does not buy the verdict and he will say so.
A Duke behind on his own charge pleads badly. Everyone knows it but the Duke.
Refused, and the Duke warned in front of the whole Mission.
The Flame does not put a family on the street in a hungry quarter.
He came for the ground and went home with a caution.
The house passes. They are roofed by the week's end.
And the roof people go too. Nobody weighed them; they were never parties to it.
Kept the years, lost the house. There is a word for that and it is not a kind one.
The courtyard beds came in heavy. There will be bread that is not the Mission's.
Good ground, well turned. The atrium keeps its own larder and it is full.
Every bed cut and carried. Nobody in this compound eats thin this quarter.
Nobody turned the beds. What came up was not worth the carrying.
Neglected ground pays neglected. The larder is a shelf and a smell.
Two beds dead and the third not worth cutting. That is a hungry quarter starting.
The larder is out. There is the Mission, and after the Mission there is the Gullet.
Thin quarter. The children eat and the rest of us watch them do it.
Alms tonight. Do not make a face about it; half this row is in the same queue.
